messages:
marcus: quick follow-up from today's mini-rfc — thinking about centralizing the 'gate coordinator' that sequences smoke/perf/compat checks for new model ingestion. how do we want to surface failures and retries?
carla: +1 on centralizing. main worry is coupling — we shouldn't make coordinator a single blocking path that can take down ingest. prefer async with backpressure. :thinking: 
jun: agree with async. also we need deterministic smoke runs so downstream rollouts can rely on a stable pass/fail signal. flaky smoke means false rejections.
priya: on retries: differentiate transient infra errors (retry) vs deterministic incompatibilities (no retry). we should record the final failure type in metadata so ops/owners can triage.
tomas: sequencing idea: run smoke first (fast), then perf and compat in parallel. if smoke fails, abort quickly. if smoke passes but perf times out, autos-fallback to smaller quantized variant for canary.
marcus: perf parallelization is appealing but increases resource contention. thought: coordinator gives tokens for heavy stages (perf, compat) to limit concurrency per cluster. simple token-bucket queue.
carla: +1 token-bucket. also want per-model priority — enterprise customers get faster tokens. add priority field in the enqueue request.
jun: what about observability? we need traceable per-stage spans and a single composite status that the model registry consumes.
priya: composite status states: queued -> running:{smoke,perf,compat} -> passed|failed. include per-stage artifacts: logs, perf-report.json, compat-diff.txt.
marcus: config sketch: ```yaml
gate_coordinator:
  stages: [smoke, perf, compat]
  strategy: parallel
  timeout_s: 600
  concurrency_tokens: 50
  priorities: {free:1, standard:5, enterprise:20}
  retry_on: [transient_network, infra_oom]
```
marcus: also thinking about synchronous vs async API for callers: registry should POST and get an admission id back (async). callback/webhook when composite status reaches terminal. synchronous endpoints for low-latency demos only.
tomas: agree on async default. demos can use a small 'quick-smoke' synchronous path that returns hint states but not full perf/compat.
carla: compatibility checks: we need to version the runtime shim used to run compat tests so results are reproducible. record runtime-fingerprint in artifacts.
jun: and bench harness should snapshot model input distributions for perf consistency. otherwise numbers drift.
priya: tradeoff: making coordinator stateful simplifies retries but complicates HA. maybe implement coordinator as stateless workers driven by a persistent job queue (postgres + leader election for cleanup). workers reconcile jobs idempotently.
marcus: yeah prefer workers + job queue. leader only for periodic cleanup and orphan detection. keep core state in job record so restarts are safe.
marcus: infra-bot: deploy check for gate-coordinator: staging cluster, 3 replicas, env GATE_TOKENS=30
infra-bot: ci: integration tests bumped; smoke harness simulated; all tests green.
priya: open question: how do we handle partial pass? example: smoke+compat pass, perf fails but within fallback thresholds. should registry mark admission as 'degraded' or 'failed'?
tomas: propose status enum: passed, degraded (allowed with policy), failed. degraded includes reason and recommended fallback model variant.
carla: policy example should be editable per-namespace. ops teams can set thresholds. small config: ```json
{"allow_degraded": true, "perf_p99_ms": 200, "degraded_variant": "quant-8"}
```
marcus: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with these tradeoffs and API sketches. priya + carla to review for HA and policy semantics. jun to add observability/span requirements. tomas will prototype token-bucket worker logic.
priya: ack, will review RFC by EOD Friday.
carla: I can take the compat runtime fingerprinting story.
jun: I'll write the perf harness snapshot proposal.
marcus: thanks all — closing thread. I'll create RFC PR and link back. :thumbsup:
